draft.title: Campaigns to save Tasmanian rivers
card: Lake Pedder
In 1972 the Tasmanian government flooded Lake Pedder to make a larger lake for hydro-electric power. Many people were angry that a wild place had been lost.
The loss spurred activists to form groups, such as the Tasmanian Wilderness Society, to save other wild places. Their next target was a plan to dam the Franklin River.
Franklin blockade
In 1982 and 1983, protesters blocked the dam works by camping on the river and getting in the way of machines. Many were arrested. Their campaign drew national attention.
High Court
In 1983 the High Court of Australia ruled that the federal government could stop the dam. The Franklin River was saved.
draft.remember: Lake Pedder was lost, which spurred activists. The Franklin blockade and the 1983 High Court ruling then stopped the dam.

a.q: How did the flooding of Lake Pedder affect the later campaign to save the Franklin River?
opts: It spurred activists to organise to save other wild places
It showed the public that dams were always a good idea
It led the High Court to ban all dams in Tasmania
It ended the work of environment groups in Tasmania
a.why: The loss of Lake Pedder made many people angry and led activists to form groups to protect other places, such as the Franklin. The High Court did not ban all dams: its 1983 ruling was about the Franklin dam.
a.clue: Think about how people felt after losing the lake.

b.q: Dana says the Franklin Dam was stopped only because protesters blocked the machines. Which reply best fits the history?
opts: The blockade won attention, but the High Court ruling stopped it
The blockade stopped it, and the High Court ruling came first
The High Court ruling stopped it, and the blockade did nothing
The Tasmanian government chose to stop it before any protest
b.why: The blockade drew national attention and many arrests, but it was the 1983 High Court ruling that let the federal government stop the dam. The blockade came first, so the second option has the order wrong.
b.clue: Which event made the legal decision to stop the dam?
